text: I enjoy building, assembling or fixing things.
I like finding out why things happen and how they work.
I enjoy creating drawings, designs, stories, videos or other original work.
I enjoy helping someone who is having difficulty.
I like taking the lead when a group needs to make a decision.
I enjoy arranging things neatly and keeping information organised.
I would enjoy using tools, equipment or practical materials to make something.

I enjoy imagining new designs, stories, characters or ideas.

I enjoy making lists, schedules or plans.

I enjoy difficult puzzles and problems that make me think.
I enjoy thinking of new or unusual ways to do things.
I like working with people and helping a team succeed.
I would enjoy starting a small project, club or team activity.

I enjoy practical outdoor activities such as making, growing, caring for or improving things.
When I do not know an answer, I enjoy searching for information to solve it.
I enjoy expressing ideas through art, design, writing, music, performance or media.
I enjoy listening to people and helping them feel supported.
I enjoy organising people so a group can reach a goal.
I enjoy following a clear system so a task is completed correctly.

I like comparing clues or evidence before deciding on an answer.
I enjoy changing or improving something so it feels more original or expressive.
I would enjoy teaching or guiding a younger student in something I know.

I enjoy sorting records, collections or information into a useful order.
When I have a difficult problem, I can break it into smaller steps.
I can explain an idea clearly so another person understands it.
I can usually think of more than one solution to a problem.
I can imagine how something might look before it is built or drawn.
I can follow steps to build, test or assemble a simple object or project.
I can usually notice when another person is uncomfortable, upset or left out.
When a group does not know how to begin, I can help everyone get started.
I can organise my work when I have several things to finish.
If my first solution does not work, I can try a different approach.
I can tell or write information in a clear order.
I can often think of a new way to improve or use an ordinary idea.
Maps, diagrams, shapes and layouts are usually easy for me to understand.
When a simple device does not work, I can think of sensible things to check first.
I work well with people who have different ideas from mine.
I can encourage other people to work toward a shared goal.
I can keep working even when there are distractions around me.
Before choosing a solution, I can compare different options and think about what may happen.
When I do not understand someone, I can ask questions to make the meaning clearer.
I can connect ideas from different places to create something new.
I can mentally picture where parts, shapes or objects would fit together.
I can use simple tools or materials carefully and follow safety instructions.
I can share tasks fairly and contribute my part when working in a team.
If something useful needs to be done, I can suggest a next step instead of waiting for someone else.
I can plan my time so important school tasks are finished by their deadline.

When something interests me, I want to know more about it.
When something is difficult, I usually keep trying.
If one method does not work, I can change my approach.
If I see something useful that needs to be done, I can begin without always waiting to be told.
I listen to other people's ideas even when they are different from mine.
I usually check my work before saying it is finished.
I can learn some new things by exploring examples or resources on my own.
I often ask 'why?' or 'how?' because I want to understand things better.
After making a mistake or failing at something, I usually try again.
I can adjust when rules, plans or situations unexpectedly change.
I am comfortable suggesting an idea when a group needs one.
I try to help my teammates succeed, not only myself.
I often notice small mistakes or details that other people miss.
When I do not understand something, I try books, examples, videos or other resources before giving up.
I enjoy asking questions that help me understand a topic more deeply.
If a task takes longer than expected, I can keep working until I make progress.
When I receive useful feedback, I can change what I am doing and try again.
When I notice a problem, I can suggest a sensible action instead of only waiting for others.
When working in a group, I can change my own idea if another idea works better.
Before submitting work, I can check important instructions and small details.
If I am curious about something, I can find a suitable way to learn more about it.
When a team is unsure what to do next, I am comfortable helping the group choose a direction.
After a setback, I usually make another attempt instead of stopping immediately.
When something surprises me, I usually want to investigate what caused it.
Before starting several tasks, I usually decide what needs to be done first.
